changes.before: Amphibians have moist skin and young that live in water (tadpoles); reptiles have dry scales and lay shelled eggs on land.
changes.after: For the supplied frog/lizard contrast, use moist skin and aquatic tadpoles for the frog, and dry scales for the lizard. Many familiar reptiles lay shelled eggs on land, but not all reptiles do; do not teach egg-laying as a universal reptile rule or as the sole classification test.
